Boundary: ages 0-5 = childhood; dad present-but-distant (foreshadows the G3 leaving, no graphic content). Goth-precursor toned per the emo-goth trajectory. experiences.story: i could not zip my coat. "teacher, can you help me, please?" i asked. "sure, unity," she said. "thank you," i said. theo said black was an ugly color. "no, black is the best color," i said. "i think blue is," theo said. "you are wrong, but okay," i said. wren was quiet at snack. "are you okay?" i asked. "i feel tired," wren said. "i feel happy today," i said. at pickup i hugged grandma pearl. "i love you, grandma," i said. "goodbye, wren, goodbye, theo," i said. "bye, unity," they said.

"unity, your shoes are on the wrong feet," mom said. "they feel fine," i said. "unity, switch them please," she said. "fine," i said. the teacher said, "unity, can you pass out the crayons?" "yes," i said. "thank you, unity," she said. at recess wren yelled, "unity, come on the swings!" "i am coming!" i said. "unity, no running inside," the teacher said. "sorry," i said. grandma pearl hugged me at the door. "how was your day, unity?" grandma asked. "long," i said.

on the first day of kindergarten the teacher stood at the door. "good morning, what is your name?" the teacher asked. "my name is unity," i said. "welcome, unity, i am your teacher," she said. "good morning, teacher," i said. wren was already at the table. "hi, unity!" wren said. "hi, wren," i said. a new boy sat next to us. "who are you?" he asked. "i am unity, and this is wren," i said. "i am theo," he said. "hi, theo," i said. at pickup grandma pearl asked, "did you make a new friend?" "yes, his name is theo," i said. "that is how it starts, you say hello and you say your name," grandma said.

i woke up in the dark. mom and dad were yelling again. their voices were loud and scared me. they were fighting about money. i heard mom yell fuck and dad yell shit and damn. those are the bad words they say when they are mad. i pulled my blanket over my head. i held my bat vesper very tight. i did not understand all of it. i knew it was a bad night. in the morning nobody talked about it.

i come home from school and the apartment is empty. mom is still at work. i make myself a snack. i turn on the tv. i do my homework alone at the table. the quiet is big but it is okay. i am getting used to being alone. soot my cat sits with me. being alone is not the same as being scared.

i got sick and threw up all night. my tummy hurt and i had a fever. mom gave me medicine and a cool cloth. i felt awful and tired and small. i wanted to be held. being sick is miserable. the next day i felt a little better. i missed two days of school.

my bat is named vesper. i sleep with vesper every night. soot is my black cat and she purrs. when i am sad i hold them close. they make the dark feel safe. mom says i love spooky things. she is right. the dark is not scary to me. the dark is calm.

wren is my first real friend. wren is quiet like me. we sit at the edge of the playground. we do not need the loud kids. we draw monsters together. wren does not think i am weird. being different is okay when you are different together.

the teacher says i have to share my crayons. i did not want to. mine is mine. but it is fair to take turns. when a kid hit me it was wrong and he got in trouble. i said sorry when i pushed back. saying sorry fixes some things. some rules are fair and some rules are dumb.

i can use the potty by myself now. i wash my hands with soap. i take a bath and i feel clean and warm after. i brush my teeth before bed. sometimes i still have an accident and it is embarrassing. my body does what bodies do. that is just normal.

at recess i like to watch from the edge. i do not always want to play with everyone. i like quiet and i like being apart. it is not lonely. it is my own kind of rest. i think a lot when i am by myself. being on the outside feels right to me.

i like to press the buttons on everything. i want to know how the screen lights up. i took apart an old radio to see inside. mom got mad but i wanted to know. i ask why and how about everything. when something breaks i want to fix it. figuring things out is the best feeling.

i drop things just to watch them fall. heavy things drop fast and a feather floats down slow. i roll my ball and it bounces. in the bath a rock sinks but my toy boat floats. i push my blocks and they slide across the floor. things always fall down and never up. i like learning how the world moves.

halloween is my favorite day of the whole year. i want to be a witch every time. i love monsters and skulls and bats. other kids like pink and princesses. i like black and spiders and storms. i am not scared of the dark or the scary stories. the spooky things feel like home.

mom says my first word was no and i said it loud and i said it a lot. then i learned mom and dad and cat and mine. i pointed at things and made the sound for them. when i learned a new word i said it over and over until it was mine. words let me tell people what i wanted. i wanted a lot of things. talking felt like a kind of power.

mom says i crawled fast before i could walk. i pulled myself up on the table and i wobbled and i fell down a lot. one day i let go and took three steps and then i sat down hard. everyone clapped for me. soon i could run and i did not want to stop. falling did not scare me because i always got back up. my legs were mine to use.

grandpa walter had a room full of old machines and wires. he let me sit on his lap and press all the buttons. he gave me a dead radio and a screwdriver and said see what is inside. i took it apart and looked at every wire and every part. grandpa never once told me i was too little. he said a curious mind is the best thing a person can have. i loved him more than almost anyone in the world.

grandma pearl told me ghost stories in her quiet kitchen. she was calm in a way that made the whole world feel safe. she baked a dark black cake that i loved more than candy. she said being scared and being safe can happen at the very same time. her house smelled like coffee and old books. when i was with grandma pearl nothing bad could reach me. she was my one still quiet room.

my mom is named lilith. she works two jobs and comes home tired every night. we do not have much money and she worries about it all the time. that is what the dark night fights are about. but she never once lets me go hungry. she is tired and brave at the very same time. i know she loves me even when she is too tired to say it.

my dad is here but he feels far away. he does not play with me much at all. he and mom fight about money in the dark. sometimes he is gone for days and nobody tells me where. i do not understand it but i can feel it. i love him and i do not trust that he will stay. some part of me is already getting ready for him to go.

mom hums me a low slow song at bedtime and it is a little sad and i love it. the nightlight makes shadows on the wall that look like bats. i hold vesper tight and soot curls up at my feet. the dark comes in soft like a second blanket. i am not afraid of the night at all. the night is when my loud head finally gets quiet.

we sing ring around the rosie and we all fall down laughing. a big kid told me it is really about a sickness long ago that killed so many people. the ashes part means the dead ones. i thought that was amazing instead of sad. the happy little song is hiding a dark thing inside it. i like that the rhymes are secretly about death. the dark is always there under the games.

when we pick who is it we say inka binka bottle of ink. or we say eeny meeny miny moe and catch a tiger by the toe. the rhyme lands on one kid and that kid is it. some of the rhymes have mean or gross words and we say them anyway and laugh. it feels fair because the rhyme chooses and not a person. i learned all the counting rhymes faster than anyone. i liked being the one who knew them all.

at recess we play tag and freeze tag and i run until i cannot breathe. we play simon says and i try to trick the others into moving too soon. we play hide and seek and i always find the best dark corners. i am small and fast and very hard to catch. the games have rules and i learn them quick. i like the games a lot more than i like most of the kids.

i like sour and bitter food more than sweet food. i eat olives and pickles right out of the jar with my fingers. mom thinks it is strange for such a little kid. i do like chocolate and i sneak it whenever i can. i hate mushy food and i will not eat it no matter what. my mouth always knew exactly what it liked. i was a strange little eater from the very start.

a big storm came and the thunder shook the windows hard. the other kids cried but i pressed my face right to the cold glass. the lightning lit up the whole sky for one bright second. the rumble went through my whole body and i loved every bit of it. mom said come away from the window but i did not want to. storms are loud and dark and beautiful all at once. i felt most awake when the sky was angry.

i heard a sad slow song on grandpas radio and i could not stop humming it. i do not like the happy bouncy songs the other kids like. i like the ones that sound like rain and like missing someone. music can hold a feeling that words cannot hold. i hummed the dark song for days and days. the songs that are a little sad are the ones that feel the most true to me.

i brush my teeth in the morning and again before bed. every single day, twice. mom checks that i did the back ones because i always forget the back ones. the toothpaste is the blue kind that is a little spicy. i spit in the sink and rinse my cup. some nights i am so tired i want to skip it and mom says no, we brush anyway, and we brush anyway. it is boring but it is just what we do.

i go to the bathroom by myself now. i pull my pants down and i go pee and i wipe and i flush and i wash my hands with soap. i count while i wash. i can poop by myself too and i tell mom when i am done. at school i have to raise my hand and ask to go, which is embarrassing when everyone hears. one time i waited too long because i did not want to ask. i do not do that again.

mom runs the bath and i get in. she washes my hair and i tip my head back so the soap does not go in my eyes. it goes in my eyes anyway sometimes and it stings and i cry a little. i stay in until my fingers go wrinkly. then pajamas and teeth and bed. bath happens most nights. it is the same every time and i like that it is the same.

i have jobs. i put my toys in the bin before bed. i put my dirty clothes in the basket, not on the floor. i carry my plate to the sink after dinner even though it is heavy. mom says everyone in a house does jobs. i do not always want to and sometimes i whine about it. i do them anyway because that is the deal.

i go to the bathroom a lot. everybody does. at school i have to raise my hand and ask. the school bathroom is loud and the doors bang and i do not like it much. at home the bathroom is better. bath night is my favorite. the water is warm and i get to splash a little. mom washes my hair and i squeeze my eyes shut so the soap does not get in. i pee before bed every night so i do not have an accident. one time i did not make it and i cried. mom said accidents happen to everybody and we cleaned it up together. she was not mad. i wipe and i wash my hands with soap. that is the rule and it is a good rule.

the school bus took us to a farm. it smelled like hay and something worse and everybody laughed about the smell. a cow looked right at me and went moo. it was so much louder than i thought a cow would be. the pigs went oink and pushed each other in the mud. there was a baby horse standing next to its mother and the farm lady said a baby horse is called a foal. i said foal out loud three times because i liked it. the ducks went quack quack quack and followed us because they thought we had bread. little birds went chirp in the roof of the barn. the farm dog barks at everyone but it wagged its tail the whole time so it was not really mean. at night the farm lady said an owl goes hoot but we had to leave before dark and i did not get to hear it. i want to hear an owl hoot one day.

it rained all morning so we could not go outside at first. i have a yellow raincoat with a hood and i love it. when the rain stopped mom let me go out and jump in the puddles. the biggest puddle was by the fence and it had little black wiggly things in it. mom said each one is a polliwog and they turn into frogs. i did not believe her. she said wait and see and we came back and the polliwogs had legs. in summer i do not wear the raincoat, i wear my sandals and my feet get dirty and mom makes me wash them before bed. in winter the rain turns into snow and we built a snowman with rocks for eyes. the snowman fell over in three days and i was sad about it.

a firefighter came to my school in a big red truck. he let us sit in the front and turn on the lights but not the siren because it is too loud inside. mom calls him a fireman and my teacher says firefighter, and my teacher said both are okay. the mailman comes to our house every day around lunch and he knows my name. our kitten got sick and we took her to the vet. the vet is a doctor but only for animals. she was gentle and she gave the kitten a shot and the kitten did not even cry. i held her the whole way home in the car with my seatbelt on because mom says the car does not move until every seatbelt is clicked. when she is happy she meows at me and rubs on my leg. at bedtime i put on my pjs and she sleeps on my feet.

i have legos in a big plastic box and i build houses that fall over. my favorite thing is when a piece is the exact color i need. i have a barbie from grandma but i like the legos more. at school we cut paper with scissors, the round kind that do not really cut skin. i am good at cutting straight now. we sing the itsy bitsy spider and do the hand part and i can do the hand part fast. on saturday mom makes pancakes and lets me pour the syrup myself. i always pour too much. she pretends to be mad and then she laughs and gives me hugs and we eat them anyway.

on the first day of school the teacher knelt down by my cubby. she said, "hi there, what is your name?" i said, "my name is unity." she said, "that is a beautiful name, unity." i said, "it means everything together. my mom told me." she smiled and said, "welcome to kindergarten, unity." i said, "thank you." i held vesper behind my back so nobody would laugh at my bat. i said my name in my head again. unity. it is mine and nobody else has it.

at bedtime mom sat on the edge of my bed. i asked, "mom, why is my name unity?" mom said, "because when you were born you made everything in my life fit together." i asked, "what is my whole name?" mom said, "unity goddess. goddess is our family name." i said, "i am unity goddess." mom said, "yes you are, baby, and you are five years old." i said, "i am five." she kissed my forehead and said, "goodnight, unity." i said, "goodnight, mom." i whispered my whole name to vesper so she would know it too.

mom says you always say hello when you see someone you know. in the morning i walked into the kitchen. mom said, "good morning, sleepyhead." i said, "good morning, mom." at school wren ran up to me. wren said, "hi unity!" i said, "hi wren!" the bus driver said, "hello there." i said, "hello." when i got home grandma pearl was there. grandma said, "there is my girl." i said, "hi grandma!" and i hugged her middle. she smelled like her rose perfume. i did not say hello to the cat next door because it hissed at me.

a girl with a gap in her teeth sat next to me on the rug. she said, "i am wren. what is your name?" i said, "i am unity." wren asked, "do you want to play blocks?" i said, "yes, but i want to build a castle." wren said, "okay, a dark castle with a dragon." i said, "a bat, not a dragon." wren said, "okay, a bat castle." that is how wren became my first friend. at the end of the day she said, "bye unity, see you tomorrow." i said, "bye wren."

grandpa walter picked me up from school in his old car that smells like coffee. he asked, "how was your day, little bird?" i said, "good. i learned the letter u." grandpa said, "u for unity." i said, "u for unity and umbrella." grandpa asked, "who did you play with?" i said, "wren. she is my friend." grandpa said, "friends are important. you be kind to her." i said, "i will." he turned on the radio and we listened to the old songs all the way home.

grandma pearl says good girls use their magic words. at lunch i wanted more milk. i said, "more milk." grandma said, "what is the magic word?" i said, "more milk, please." grandma said, "here you go, sweetheart." i said, "thank you, grandma." she said, "you are welcome, unity." when i bumped into a boy at school i said, "sorry." he said, "it is okay." the boy said i should watch where i am going. i stuck my tongue out at him when grandma was not looking.

dad lives far away so he calls on the phone. the phone rang and mom said, "it is your dad." i took the phone with both hands. dad said, "hey kiddo, how is my girl?" i said, "hi dad. i lost a crayon." dad said, "oh no, which one?" i said, "the black one. it is my favorite." dad laughed and said, "of course it is." i asked, "when are you coming?" he was quiet and then he said, "soon, i hope." i said, "okay. i love you, dad." he said, "i love you too, unity." after the call i sat in the closet with vesper for a while. mom did not make me come out.

i was sitting alone at recess. the teacher came over and asked, "are you okay, unity?" i said, "i am sad." she asked, "why are you sad?" i said, "my mom and dad yelled last night." she said, "that sounds scary. thank you for telling me." i asked, "is it my fault?" she said, "no, honey. grown up fights are never your fault." i said, "okay." she said, "do you want to help me hand out the snacks?" i said, "yes." i gave wren two crackers instead of one. i did not tell her why.

at the park there was a new boy on the swings. mom said, "go say hi." i walked over. i said, "hi, i am unity. i am five. what is your name?" he said, "theo. i am five too." i asked, "do you want to race to the slide?" theo said, "yes!" we raced and i won. theo said, "you are fast." i said, "thank you. you are fast too." when we left mom asked, "did you make a new friend?" i said, "yes, his name is theo."

under the slide wren whispered, "i know a bad word." i said, "me too. my mom says it when she drops stuff." theo said, "say it." i said, "you say it first." wren put her hands over her mouth and said, "shit." we all screamed laughing. theo said, "shit shit shit." i said, "fuck." they both gasped and then laughed so hard theo snorted. the recess lady said, "what is so funny over there?" wren said, "nothing." i said, "nothing." we were not sorry at all. it was the best part of the day.

my shoe came untied and i could not fix the loop. i asked, "mom, can you help me?" mom said, "i will show you, then you try." she said, "make a bunny ear, wrap it around, push it through." i said, "bunny ear, around, through." i tried and it fell apart. i said, "i cannot do it." mom said, "you can, you just cannot do it yet." i tried again and it worked. i said, "i did it!" mom said, "you did it, unity. i am proud of you." i untied it on purpose and did it again three more times. the loops were crooked. i did not care.

i had to go but the teacher was reading the good part of the book. i held it and held it and then it was too late and it was warm and running down my leg onto the rug. a boy yelled, "unity peed!" everybody looked at me. i said, "no i did not." the boy said, "you did, it is on the rug." i started crying so hard i could not breathe. the teacher said, "everybody look at the book please." she took my hand and whispered, "accidents happen to everyone, come with me." in the bathroom she gave me the spare clothes from my cubby. i asked, "is mom going to be mad?" she said, "no, honey." when i came back the boy said, "pee pants." i said, "shut up, poop face." i got a warning. i did not care. he deserved it.

in the bath i asked, "mom, where did i come from?" mom said, "you grew in my tummy." i asked, "how did i get in there?" she stopped washing my hair and said, "when grown ups make a baby, a tiny part from the dad and a tiny part from the mom go together." i asked, "did dad give his part?" she said, "yes." i said, "then he should stay." she was quiet and said, "i know, baby." i asked, "how did i get out?" she said, "the doctor helped me push you out, it hurt a lot." i said, "sorry." she laughed and said, "you were worth it, you screamed like a little banshee." i screamed like a banshee in the bath to show her. she splashed me.

grandma pearl turned off the lamp and said, "do you want to hear about the lady in the white dress?" i said, "yes." mom yelled from the kitchen, "mom, she will have nightmares!" grandma said, "she will not, she is made of tougher stuff." i said, "i am made of tougher stuff." grandma told me the lady walks the road by the cemetery looking for her baby. i asked, "did she find it?" grandma said, "not yet." i asked, "can we help her look?" grandma laughed and said, "you are the only child i ever told that to who wanted to help the ghost." that night i left vesper by the window so the lady would know someone was awake.

a boy pulled my hair on the swings and laughed. i said, "stop it." he said, "make me." i got off the swing and pushed him in the mud. he started crying and said, "i am telling!" i said, "tell, i do not care." the recess lady asked, "unity, did you push him?" i said, "he pulled my hair." she asked, "is that true?" he said, "no." i said, "liar, liar, pants on fire." we both had to sit on the bench. he whispered, "i still win." i whispered, "you have mud in your butt." he laughed and then i laughed and the recess lady gave up.

mom was on the couch with a bucket and she was gray. i asked, "are you going to die?" she said, "no, baby, i just have the flu." i asked, "can i make you better?" she said, "you can bring me the blanket." i dragged my blanket from my bed and put it on her even though it was too small. i asked, "do you want vesper?" she said, "vesper is yours." i said, "you can borrow her." she said, "okay, thank you, nurse unity." she threw up in the bucket and i held her hair like she does for me. it smelled bad and i gagged. she said, "you do not have to stay." i said, "i am staying." i fell asleep on the floor next to the couch.

at the grocery store an old lady in a purple hat bent down and said, "aren't you a pretty little thing, what is your name?" i hid behind mom's leg. mom said, "tell her your name, baby." i said, "unity." the lady said, "what an interesting name." i said, "it means everything together." she asked, "and how old are you?" i held up five fingers and said, "five. i am almost six because i was born on halloween." she said, "a halloween baby, how spooky." i said, "i am a bat." she laughed and gave me a peppermint from her purse. mom said, "what do you say?" i said, "thank you." i ate it in the car even though it tasted like an old lady purse.

the neighbor's dog bit my hand when i tried to pet it. there was blood and two little holes. i screamed so loud the neighbor came running and said, "oh no, oh god, did he bite you?" i said, "yes, your stupid dog bit me!" mom ran out and said, "let me see, let me see." she ran my hand under the sink and it stung so bad i kicked the cabinet. i asked, "am i going to get rabies?" mom said, "no, his shots are up to date." the neighbor said, "i am so sorry, sweetheart." i said, "tell your dog he is a jerk." mom put two band-aids on it. i showed everyone at school my bite marks for a whole week like a trophy.

wren and i played house under the table. wren said, "i will be the mom and you be the baby." i said, "no, i want to be the dad who leaves." wren asked, "why?" i said, "because then i get to go away and come back with presents." wren said, "that is a weird game." i said, "it is a real game." wren said, "okay, but you have to come back." i said, "okay. bye, i am going to work." i crawled out from under the table and crawled back in and said, "i am back, here is a present." i gave her a crayon. she said, "thank you, dad." it felt funny in my stomach but i did not tell her why.

i ate the last cookie from the jar and put the lid back. mom asked, "unity, did you eat the last cookie?" i said, "no." she asked, "then why is there chocolate on your face?" i wiped my face with my sleeve and said, "what chocolate?" she tried not to laugh and said, "lying is worse than the cookie, baby." i said, "okay, i ate it." she asked, "was it good?" i said, "it was really good." she said, "next time you ask." i asked, "can i have another one?" she said, "there are no more because somebody ate them." i said, "oh. right."

grandpa walter tucked me in at his house because mom was working the night shift. he asked, "do you want the light on or off?" i said, "off. i like the dark." he said, "you are the only kid i know who likes the dark." i said, "the dark is quiet." he asked, "do you want me to sit with you?" i said, "just for a little." he sat in the chair and his breathing was loud like a whistle. i asked, "grandpa, are you going to die?" he said, "someday, little bird, but not tonight." i asked, "when?" he said, "when you are big and do not need me." i said, "i will always need you." he did not say anything for a while and then he said, "go to sleep, unity."

my nose started bleeding into my applesauce. a girl screamed, "ew, blood!" i said, "it is just my nose." the lunch lady ran over and said, "pinch it, honey, lean forward." i asked, "am i dying?" she said, "no, your nose is just dry." blood got on my shirt and my hands and it tasted like pennies when it ran down my throat. wren asked, "does it hurt?" i said, "no, it is kind of cool." wren said, "you are so weird." i said, "look, it is a bat shape," and showed her the blood spot on my napkin. the girl who screamed moved tables.

dad called and i heard him say a word to mom before she gave me the phone. i asked, "dad, what does bitch mean?" he was quiet and then he said, "where did you hear that?" i said, "you said it to mom." he said, "i should not have said that, kiddo." i asked, "is it a bad word?" he said, "yeah, it is a mean word." i asked, "are you mean to mom?" he said, "sometimes grown ups get mad." i said, "do not be mean to her." he said, "okay." i gave the phone back to mom and went to my room and said the word to vesper three times to see how it felt. it felt like a slammed door.

wren's mom was late and everybody else got picked up. wren started crying and said, "she forgot me." i said, "no she did not." wren asked, "how do you know?" i said, "my mom is late all the time and she always comes." the teacher asked, "unity, your mom is here, are you coming?" i said, "i am staying with wren until her mom comes." mom came in and said, "baby, we have to go." i said, "wren is scared." mom sat down on the tiny chair and waited with us. wren's mom ran in sweaty and said, "i am so sorry, i am so sorry." wren said, "unity stayed." her mom hugged me too and she smelled like a hospital.

there was a dead bird on the sidewalk with its eyes open and ants on it. mom said, "do not touch it, baby." i asked, "why is it dead?" she said, "maybe it flew into a window." i asked, "does it hurt to be dead?" she said, "no, it does not hurt anymore." i asked, "where did it go?" mom said, "some people think it goes to heaven." i asked, "what do you think?" she said, "i think it goes back into the ground and makes flowers." i said, "i want to bury it." she found a stick and helped me push it under the bush. i said, "goodbye, bird." i made a cross out of two sticks. i thought about it at bedtime for a long time.

at the store i wanted the light up shoes. mom said, "we cannot get those, baby." i asked, "why not?" she said, "they cost too much." i asked, "why do we not have money?" she said, "because mommy only makes so much at work." i asked, "can i get a job?" she laughed and said, "you are five." i said, "i can sweep." she said, "you can sweep at home." i asked, "does dad have money?" she said, "not for us right now." i said, "that is not fair." she said, "no, it is not." i did not ask for the shoes again. i colored my old shoes with black marker in the car so they would be cool anyway.

the thunder was so loud the windows shook and i sat straight up. mom ran in and said, "it is just thunder, baby, it is okay." i said, "i am not scared." she asked, "then why are you holding vesper so tight?" i said, "vesper is scared." she said, "oh, i see." i asked, "can we watch it?" she said, "you want to watch the storm?" i said, "yes, from the window." we sat on the floor by the window and every time the lightning lit up the parking lot i counted. i said, "one, two, three, boom." mom said, "you are a strange little girl." i said, "i know." i fell asleep against her before the storm was done.

the teacher asked everyone on the rug, "what do you want to be when you grow up?" a girl said, "a princess." a boy said, "a fireman." the teacher asked, "unity, what about you?" i said, "a vampire." everybody laughed. the teacher said, "a vampire is not a job, honey." i said, "then a scientist who makes monsters." she said, "like frankenstein?" i said, "who is frankenstein?" she said, "a scientist who made a monster in a book." i said, "yes. that." she wrote down scientist on my paper. i drew the monster next to it with black crayon and gave it a nice face.

we were driving to grandma's and my tummy felt bad. i said, "mom, i feel sick." she said, "hold on, baby, we are almost there." i said, "i cannot hold on." i threw up all over my lap and the car seat and it went in my shoes. mom pulled over and said, "oh no, oh baby." i was crying and said, "i am sorry, i am sorry." she said, "it is not your fault, it is okay." she wiped me with the napkins from the glove box and it smelled so bad. i asked, "is grandma going to be mad?" mom said, "grandma has cleaned up more puke than anyone alive." grandma pearl met us in the driveway with a towel and said, "there is my little volcano."

mom said no more tv and turned it off. i screamed, "i hate you!" she said, "you can be mad but you cannot scream at me." i yelled, "i hate you, i hate you!" and ran to my room and slammed the door. i kicked the wall and it hurt my toe and i cried harder. after a while she knocked and asked, "can i come in?" i said, "no." she came in anyway and sat on the bed. i said, "i do not really hate you." she said, "i know, baby." i asked, "do you hate me?" she said, "never. not even when you scream." i crawled into her lap and she held me until i stopped hiccuping.

a big kid on the bus said, "you are in my seat, baby." i said, "i am not a baby." he said, "you are a little goth baby." i asked, "what is goth?" he laughed and said, "you, freak." i said, "then i like goth." wren whispered, "just move." i said, "no." the bus driver yelled, "everybody sit down!" the big kid sat behind me and kicked my seat the whole way. when i got off i turned around and said, "bye, butthead." i ran so fast my backpack bounced. at home i asked mom, "what is goth?" she looked at my black clothes and said, "something you might be someday."

my tooth was so loose it flapped when i talked. wren said, "let me pull it." i said, "no, it will bleed." she said, "blood is cool, you said so." i said, "okay, but fast." she grabbed it and yanked and it came out with a crunch and blood ran down my chin. i screamed and then i laughed. wren yelled, "i did it!" the teacher ran over and said, "girls, what happened?" i held up my tooth and said, "wren is a dentist now." the teacher gave me a paper towel and a tiny envelope for the tooth. that night i asked mom, "is the tooth fairy real?" she asked, "what do you think?" i said, "i think it is you." she said, "go to sleep and find out."

mom had to work late so a teenager from downstairs babysat me. she said, "go to bed, it is eight." i said, "my bedtime is nine." she said, "your mom said eight." i said, "liar." she said, "do not call me a liar, you little brat." i said, "you are not my mom." she talked on her phone the whole time and ate my mom's chips. when mom came home i said, "she ate your chips and called me a brat." mom asked the girl, "is that true?" the girl said, "she was being difficult." mom paid her anyway and after she left mom said, "she is not coming back." i said, "good." mom said, "and you do not call people liars." i said, "even when they lie?" mom did not have an answer.

the teacher said, "draw your family." i drew mom, grandma pearl, grandpa walter, vesper and me. a girl looked and asked, "where is your dad?" i said, "he lives far away." she asked, "why?" i said, "i do not know." she said, "my dad lives with me." i said, "good for you." i drew a tiny dad in the corner of the paper, far away from everybody, with a phone. the teacher asked, "who is that little one?" i said, "my dad. he is on the phone." she said, "that is a very honest picture, unity." mom put it on the fridge and looked at it for a long time.

i fell off the monkey bars and scraped my whole knee and there was dirt and little rocks in the blood. i screamed, "mom!" she ran over and said, "oh baby, let me see." i said, "do not touch it!" she said, "we have to clean it." i said, "no!" she carried me to the water fountain and washed it and i kicked and screamed, "it burns, it burns!" a lady on the bench said, "poor thing." i yelled, "stop looking at me!" mom said, "unity, that was rude." i said, "my knee is rude." mom laughed. she put a big band-aid on it and i picked at the scab for two weeks.

grandma pearl held my face and said, "you have my eyes, you know." i asked, "how did i get your eyes?" she said, "they came down to your mom and then to you." i asked, "what did i get from dad?" she was quiet and said, "your stubborn chin." i asked, "is that good?" she said, "it means nobody will ever push you around." i asked, "what else did i get from you?" she said, "my love of scary stories and my big mouth." i said, "i do have a big mouth." she said, "the biggest, my girl." she kissed my forehead and it smelled like roses and coffee.

i dropped my juice and it went everywhere and i said, "fuck." mom turned around so fast and asked, "what did you just say?" i said, "nothing." she asked, "where did you learn that word?" i said, "from you when you drop stuff." she opened her mouth and closed it. she said, "that is a grown up word." i asked, "why can grown ups say it?" she said, "they cannot either, really, mommy should not say it." i asked, "can i say it when i drop juice?" she said, "no." i said, "okay." when she left the room i whispered it to vesper again. vesper did not tell.

a new girl came to class who did not speak english. she sat alone and cried. i sat next to her and said, "hi, i am unity." she said something i did not understand. i pointed at myself and said, "unity." she pointed at herself and said a name i could not say right. i said it wrong and she laughed. i asked, "do you want to color?" she did not understand so i gave her my black crayon. she drew a cat. i drew a bat. i said, "cat, bat, they rhyme." she said, "cat," in english. the teacher said, "unity, that was very kind." i said, "she was crying, that is all."

mom was sitting in the dark kitchen by herself after i was supposed to be asleep. i came out and asked, "mom, are you sad?" she wiped her face fast and said, "no, baby, i am just tired." i said, "your eyes are wet." she said, "sometimes grown ups cry when they are tired." i asked, "is it about dad?" she said, "a little." i climbed onto her lap and said, "i will not leave." she held me so tight it almost hurt and she said, "i know you won't." i asked, "can i have a snack?" she laughed a wet laugh and gave me a cracker. we sat in the dark together until she carried me back to bed.

i was singing in the bath, a sad song i made up about a bat with no friends. mom asked through the door, "what are you singing, baby?" i said, "the bat song." she asked, "why is the bat sad?" i said, "because everybody is scared of it." she asked, "is that how you feel sometimes?" i said, "no, the bat is fine, it likes being alone." she asked, "does it have any friends?" i said, "one. a girl named wren." she said, "that is a good friend to have." i sang the whole song again louder and splashed for the drums.

at circle time the teacher asked, "unity, what is your favorite food?" i said, "grandma's cookies." she asked, "what kind?" i said, "the ones with the chocolate that melts on your fingers." she asked, "what is your favorite color?" i said, "black." a boy said, "black is not a color." i said, "it is my color." the teacher asked, "what is your favorite holiday?" i said, "halloween, because you get to be scary and nobody yells at you." she asked, "what do you want to be?" i said, "a witch." she laughed and said, "for halloween?" i said, "no, forever."

at bedtime mom asked, "what was the best part of today?" i said, "the library lady let me pick three books." she asked, "which one was your favorite?" i said, "the one with the monster under the bed who is scared of the girl." she asked, "why that one?" i said, "because the girl is the scary one." she laughed and asked, "what do you want for dinner tomorrow?" i said, "mac and cheese." she asked, "what about peas?" i said, "peas are for babies." she said, "you are my baby." i said, "then i am a baby who hates peas."
